claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 has inherent or significant porosity.
Conventional ZrB2 has inadequate structural integrity under prolonged liquid-plating exposure.
Adding multiple transition-metal dopants through a liquid-precursor route can create a high-entropy variant of ZrB2.
The proposed high-entropy modification can lower the required sintering temperature below 2300 °C.
The targeted preparation range for the modified ceramic is approximately 1900–2100 °C.
The high-entropy dopant mixture induces formation of a transient liquid phase during sintering.
The transient liquid phase enhances diffusion during sintering.
Enhanced diffusion caused by liquid-phase sintering improves densification at lower temperatures.
Improved densification reduces pore and defect formation.
A microstructure with fewer pores and defects improves mechanical stability during long-term liquid-plating service.
High-entropy-modified ZrB2 is expected to attain comparable or improved densification at temperatures 200–400 °C below conventional processing temperatures.
High-entropy-modified ZrB2 is expected to have comparable or improved mechanical strength relative to conventionally prepared ZrB2.
High-entropy-modified ZrB2 is expected to show lower porosity than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
High-entropy-modified ZrB2 is expected to resist failure better during extended liquid-plating exposure.
An exposure duration of about 1000 hours is proposed as an industrially relevant service boundary.
